prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign CANCER: a crab seen from the front, low and wide, its domed shell a smooth half-circle like a rising moon, two small eyes on short stalks, two large claws raised symmetrically on either side like a pair of crescent moons, legs spread evenly beneath. A full moon directly above the shell.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, concentric ripples and small wave crests spread outward past the frame; a line of tide crosses the bottom of the hexagon.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. It is an animal: absolutely NO human face, no nose, no mouth, no eyebrows on the shell. The sign's nature shows only through form: rounded, enclosing, shell-like curves: shelter, protection, the pull of the moon.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: pale silver, coral red, teal, deep blue. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
